text: Turned in best effort when keeping on third in a 1m Kempton handicap on return. Failed to improve as hoped tackling 1¼m for the first time at Salisbury a month ago. Looks worth another chance over this sort of trip, though, and handicapper has dropped her 3 lb.

Successful at Newcastle on 3 of her last handicap 4 starts, returning from a break with a straightforward success in a valuable event there on Good Friday. Confirmed her effectiveness on turf and was unlucky not to finish closer still when third in a Curragh Group 2 (1m) last month. Respected.

Wootton Bassett colt who made a winning start despite obvious inexperience in 7-runner maiden at Pontefract (6f, good) just over a fortnight ago, edging a tight finish despite going markedly right under pressure. Open to improvement.

900,000 gns breeze-up purchase who looked a very good prospect when picking off Fast Track late on to make a winning start to her career at Nottingham (5f, good to soft) 14 days ago, quickening up smartly having been denied a clear run. Open to significant improvement so lots to like.

Teofilo filly out of a Group 3 winning dam. Off the mark at the fourth attempt in a first-time hood (discarded here) in a 9-runner maiden at Dieppe last summer for H-F. Devin. Changed hands for €13,000 in February and is probably best watched making handicap debut after almost a year off.
Unreliable sort who made it 6 successive non-completions when pulled up in 17f handicap hurdle at Newton Abbot two weeks ago.

First past post in French 1000 Guineas last year but was subsequently disqualified for interference. Missed second half of last season with an injury but shaped as if retaining ability when third to Blue Bolt in Goodwood listed race on return. Poor run at Epsom since, though, and headgear goes on.

Kodi Bear colt who knew his job when landing odds in 7-runner novice at Lingfield (6f) in April. Showed plenty of ability again when second of 13 in Woodcote Stakes at Epsom (6f, good to soft) 12 days ago and he remains with potential.

Smooth winner of 17-runner handicap here in September and shaped well when fourth in the Balmoral next time. Wasn't seen to best effect on first 2 outings this season before matching the pick of last year's form when third at York in May, faring best of those ridden prominently.
Progressive filly who looked right at home stepped up to listed level when fourth at Haydock last month but likely to find this company too demanding.

Smart form at best in Australia, runner-up in 1¼m Group 1 at Randwick in October 2024. Down the field in only 2 starts early last year, but after 14 months off (had a breathing operation) he wasn't disgraced on stable debut when 2¾ lengths seventh of 12 in 7f handicap at Haydock in April.

Turned in best effort when second of 4 behind smart prospect in 5f novice at Hamilton in May. Hasn't kicked on since, including on handicap debut at Catterick last time, but yard among the winners and have decent record when applying first-time headgear. Claims if bouncing back.
Decisive bumper winner last spring but has disappointed over jumps since, including remote fourth on recent C&D chase debut (didn't convince with jumping). Tongue tied first time here.

Multiple C&D winner, including twice last year. Confirmed return to form when winning 8-runner handicap at Pontefract 15 days ago, beating Pol Roger by neck. Remains well treated on old form and must be taken seriously back at this venue.
Reached the frame on all 3 5f starts for Karl Burke, leaving that yard after finishing third in Beverley claimer 3 weeks ago. The step up to 6f looks sure to suit her.

Territories colt who made a winning start at Hamilton (6f, good to firm) last month. Towards the head of the betting but failed to handle the track when twelfth of 13 in Woodcote Stakes at Epsom (6f, good to soft) 12 days ago. First-time blinkers now reached for.

Picked up where she left off and proved better than ever after 5 months off when scoring at Kempton (6f) in April and looked back in the groove after a pair of low-key efforts when sixth of 14 at Wetherby (7f) last time. Probably up against it racing from out of the weights in this company, though.

Naval Crown colt who finished runner-up to A Bear Affair in Brocklesby Stakes at Doncaster then again filled that position in 3-runner conditions stakes at this course (5f, good to firm) early last month, just finding the better-positioned winner a bit too clued up. More needed here.

Pushed out to just hold off a fast-finishing runner-up and make it third time lucky in novice at York (5f, good) on Saturday. Faces a much stiffer task turned out again quickly. Cheekpieces are added.

Front-runner who was underwhelming over hurdles last season but back on track sent chasing when second at Wincanton in April. Clearly not himself under a change of tactics at Hereford last month and bounced straight back when second of 8 at Fontwell (2¼m, good to firm) 9 days later.
Front-runner who won 3 times over hurdles last spring. Best effort over fences when 6 lengths second to Beorma (who has won again since) over C&D (good to soft) 3 weeks ago. Considered.

All 4 wins on all-weather, the latest on reappearance at Newcastle (1m). Respectable efforts in defeat since, including when upped in trip to finish sixth of 11 in handicap at Chester (10.3f, good to firm, 66/1) 40 days ago. Others look better treated from 1 lb out of the weights.
Fair Flat winner who comes here on the back of a solid third at Brighton (1½m) 19 days ago. In excellent hands and not out of things now going hurdling.

Mohaather filly who was very green in the preliminaries prior to finishing fourth of 10 at Thirsk on debut and left that well behind with blinkers added (retained) when making all at Windsor (5f, good to firm) 16 days ago. That form is nothing special but she can improve again.
Built on promising Newmarket debut when a ready 4-length winner of a C&D novice (good to firm) 6 weeks ago. Likely to progress again but Buick switches to Senorita Bonita.

Made a winner return at Compiegne in April and proved better than ever when ¾-length second of 10 to Anakova in listed race at Longchamp (1m, soft) 34 days ago. Well drawn but probably needs a couple of her rivals to falter if she's to get seriously involved.
Successful twice over C&D in 2024 but little to enthuse about since. Requires a big leap of faith.

Fairly useful bumper scorer. Built on her hurdling debut with second of 10 in novice at Newton Abbot (17f) 21 days ago, collared late having looked likely winner. May do better still so not out of things.

Gradually progressive in handicaps last year, successful at Sandown and Southwell during the summer before only narrowly denied in the Cambridgeshire, though was well drawn. Better than ever on return when neck second of 15 to Classic at Newbury last month, but will need to find more again.

Won at Chelmsford (1m) in March and was a good second of 15 at Chester (1½m) on her penultimate outing. Would've benefited from a stronger pace when mid-field at Goodwood (1½m) last time but she's 4 lb out of the weights down markedly in trip here and surely up against it.
Yet to add to her bumper success in this sphere but she posted a good third of 7 in handicap hurdle at Ludlow (2m) last month. No forlorn hope.

Progressed well when a 4-time winner (around 7f/1m) in 2025 and confirmed herself as still on the up when taking 9-runner handicap at this C&D (good to firm) 39 days ago by 2½ lengths from Song N Dance. Had run of the race there, though, so might need more again from 6 lb higher mark.
Foaled April 17. Space Traveller half-sister to several winners, including 2-y-o 7.2f winner Elzaam Tales and 6f winner Patsy Fagan, but she was picked up for only 1,500 gns at the breeze-ups.

Consistent over hurdles without winning and gave it a good go switched to fences at Stratford (17f, good to soft) last month, going down by only a nose to one who won again next time. Likely to be bang there if in the same form.
Failed to beat a rival in a point and bumper last year and a tailed-off third of 5 in novice at Fakenham (2m) on hurdles bow 17 days ago.
A long-standing maiden on the Flat (stays 1¾m) and came in a well-held sixth of 8 on first try in this discipline at Huntingdon (2m) last month.

Fairly consistent over hurdles, landing a fourth handicap success in 8-runner event at Sedgefield (27f) last September. Given a break since finishing fourth at Chepstow (3m) the following month. Might be the one to follow Our Guide home.

Highly tried since winning a listed race at York at 2 and though she shaped as if still in decent form when 10¾ lengths fourth of 7 to Sparks Fly in Princess Elizabeth Stakes (22/1) at Epsom (8.5f, good to soft) 11 days ago, her mark looks on the stiff side having just a second handicap start.

Twice runner-up in bumpers and fair form shown in this sphere, placed for third time with solid third of 6 in novice at Stratford (19f) 18 days ago. Holds good form claims. Engaged Stratford 2.05 Tuesday.

Promise when placed at Beverley (5f, good to soft) and Newcastle (6f, all-weather) a year apart. The fact she was reported to have bled at Newcastle is a bit of a concern but still rates the obvious danger to Grasmere Boy.

Made a winning return in the Lincoln last season and improved again when following up at Newcastle in June. Wasn't in the same form on final 3 starts of the campaign, though, and having left William Haggas he fared little better at York on last month's reappearance.

Got back on the up with a strong-travelling success at York (1¼m) in May last year. Ended the season on a low-key note, but with reappearance run behind him he finished a good second in latest renewal of the same York race. Task is now to build on latest effort.

Dual handicap winner last season who found plenty of improvement when narrowly beaten in 7f listed race here in October. However, ran poorly at Lingfield on return and plenty to find even if back to her best.

Won twice last summer for William Haggas. Campaigned in Meydan for current trainer to start this year and has gone the right way with each of his 3 starts, in first-time hood when landing 14-runner handicap in March. Could go well under James McDonald.

Space Blues colt who showed promise when second of 7 in maiden at Newcastle (6f, 9/1) on debut last month, headed entering final 1f having made most. Entitled to progress but will need to do so significantly to figure.
Fairly useful winner on Flat (stays 2m). Made mistakes when a debut third over hurdles in 2m Huntingdon maiden last May. Back from 8 months off with more required.
Last on both her runs in bumpers at Newton Abbot and Chepstow (hooded) for Chris Down. Goes hurdling now for new handler after 6 months off.
Hasn't kicked on from her debut second in 6f maiden at Pontefract last summer, including in handicaps on last 2 starts. May need her mark to come down a bit more.

Patiently-ridden mare who produced a career best when landing the Dahlia Stakes at Newmarket (9f) on return, seen to good effect to reel in Cathedral. Found next run at the Curragh playing out less favourably but she's a player if they go hard here.

Well-bred Frankel colt who showed bags of promise when runner-up in a useful 1¼m Yarmouth novice on debut in April and didn't need to reproduce that form to land the odds at Newbury (1¼m) since. Looked a little less than straightforward but he's bred to stay at least 1½m and retains potential.

Winner of the Spring Cup at Newbury on last season and took his form up a notch later in the campaign, scoring over this C&D in August and going on to finish second in the Balmoral. Excuses on return before creditable 2¾ lengths fourth of 15 to Classic at Newbury last month.

Worked his way back to best this year, looking unlucky not to win when beaten a neck at Wolverhampton (7f) in February. Was left poorly placed at York and also didn't have much luck when 10¼ lengths sixth of 10 to Glory Hyde over C&D 14 days ago from a very tough track position. Looks interesting.

Landed a double over 1¼m at Pontefract last summer and he lines up here having run creditably when third in a 4-runner handicap over this trip back there 9 days ago (Something placed second). Remains 1 lb above last successful mark and others preferred for win purposes.

Easily made all in novice at Beverley (5f). Went off too hard in the Marygate at York next time but confirmed she's quite useful when ¾-length third of 8 to Where Love Lives in listed National at Sandown (5f, good) 20 days ago.

Has yet to get anywhere near his fairly useful Flat form over hurdles but better signs when third at Plumpton in January. Proved a let-down at Wetherby following month. Cheekpieces tried now after a break and handily weighted if they spark a resurgence.
Modest form on all 3 starts, runner-up on last 2, beaten 2 lengths by promising Supplicate in novice at Bath last time. Makes handicap debut with first-time cheekpieces.

Has quickly developed into a smart performer, making a successful return at Newmarket and quickly bouncing back from a lesser effort (had excuses) when overcoming interference to land 18-runner event at Epsom 12 days ago. 1 lb well-in under a penalty.
Well-bred Palace Pier colt who made it 2 wins from 3 starts in handicap company in first-time cheekpieces at Chester (1½m) last month but this demands a whole lot more.

Stepped up on debut third when short-head second of 10 to Senorita Bonita in maiden at Nottingham (5f, good to soft) 14 days ago, showing good speed. Might prove slightly flattered by her proximity to that reopposing rival but she's likely still capable of better again.

Space Blues colt who went the wrong way from his debut despite enjoying an experience edge over nearly all his rivals when fourth of 8 in maiden at Leicester (6f, firm) just over 3 weeks ago. First-time hood goes on.
Has taken well to chasing this spring, placing on first 3 attempts before making all at Hereford (2m, good) 6 weeks ago. Her jumping looks a real asset and a 4 lb rise may not stop her.

Mohaather colt who proved easy to back but knew his job when winning 13-runner maiden at the Curragh (6f, good) on debut a fortnight ago by 2 lengths from One Number, asserting final 100 yds. Entitled to progress.
Down the field in 2 outings 9 months apart (trained by Jack Channon on debut).

Successful debut in the Chesham here in 2022 and holding his form well these days, runner-up in the Balmoral in October before going one better in listed race at Kempton in December. Ran up to his best back on these shores when second in listed contest over C&D last month but this is a tall order.

Making only fourth start for current yard, returned to winning ways in Bahrain (7f) in January and followed up in good style at the same course (1m). Ran to similar level when mid-field in listed event at Doha the following month, but has work to do in this company.

Blinkered, pulled 7 lengths clear of a next-time-out winner for an impressive debut success at Churchill Downs (4.5f) 7 weeks ago. Surely more to come for American yard which knows what it takes to win this.

Form has taken off since the end of last year, recording her third win of 2026 at Carlisle last month. Left the impression recent busy spell had caught up with her when down the field at Thirsk (1m, good) 2 days later but subsequent break will help her cause. Remains of interest.

Has improved with every start in a light career to date, producing a useful effort after 10 months off to win a 5-runner handicap at Doncaster (1m, firm) 12 days ago, Big-field scenario should suit given her strong-travelling style and she enters calculations from 4 lb higher.

Has returned in tremendous heart, runner-up in the Spring Cup at Newbury before going one better in 15-runner contest at the same course in May, scoring by a neck from Indalo having typically travelled well. Can give another good account.

Kodiac filly who made it 2-2 when pipping Armor Supreme on the line in listed Marygate at York (5f, good) 33 days ago. The stiffer 5f here should see her in an even better light. Respected for yard seeking a third win in this since 2022.

Ran well when sixth of 15 in the Golden Gates at this meeting last year and made the frame in a trio of handicaps at Meydan to start 2026. Returned to winning ways with a comfortable success in 7-runner event at Bro Park in May, but this is much more competitive.

Useful form at 2 yrs, winning 1m maiden at Punchestown and finishing third in 9f Leopardstown Group 3. Showed improved form fitted with first-time cheekpieces when fifth of 10 in strong 1¼m Newbury handicap on reappearance last month, shaping as though 1½m+ will suit even better.

Shaped up well for current yard last season, including a never-nearer fourth of 23 in the Cambridgeshire when faring easily best of the stand side group. Overcame pace bias when making a winning return at Newmarket (9f) by ½ length from Fifth Column and the nature of this race should suit.

Won handicap and listed race at the Curragh last season and returned with a couple of respectable efforts, beaten 1½ lengths when mid-field in Group 3 at Saint-Cloud in March. However, below form back in Britain the last twice, including at Epsom 12 days ago. Visor reached for.
Placed 3 times last year for Roger Varian but has made very little impression in 2 runs for new yard after a breathing operation.
Useful filly but she has been found out at this level twice already this season.
Kodi Bear filly who didn't shape at all badly when third of 7 in novice at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) on debut last month. Entitled to progress but this is a completely different kettle of fish.
Progressive form, accounting for Kentucky Rain when making it third time lucky in novice at Goodwood (5f, good) 26 days ago. May do better again but it will be needed.

Won first 2 starts and bit better than the result (raced close to strong pace) when 2 lengths third of 10 to Love A Giggle and Armor Supreme in York listed event (5f, good) 33 days ago. David Egan looks elsewhere but she remains open to progress.
NON RUNNER.

Mowed down Minnie Hauk late on in last year's Arc and has looked equally as good back at Longchamp over shorter trips this spring, quickening clear for impressive 3½-length wins in the Ganay and Aga Khan. Quick ground asks a different question but he increasingly looks a colt out of the top drawer.

Has made the track only 3 times since a winning debut in October 2024 but she arguably shaped best when 2½ lengths third of 9 to Radiant Beauty in handicap at this C&D (good to firm) last month, nearest at the finish having been left with plenty to do. Can improve again and makes plenty of appeal.
Keen-going sort ended a losing run at Uttoxeter (2m) in May and backed it up with a solid third of 5 in handicap there (2m) 13 days ago. Possibilities.
Hinted at promise with fourth in juvenile at Ludlow in December but tongue tied and came in a remote third of 6 in 2m Huntingdon novice 23 days ago. Needs to bounce back.
Confirmed her debut promise when winning the 8-runner Hilary Needler at Beverley (5f, good to firm) 18 days ago. Open to improvement for a stable which has tasted 2-y-o success at this meeting.

Progressed into a high-class filly last year, winning Oaks, Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks before close second to Daryz in the Arc. Completed a simple task in Curragh Group 2 on reappearance and subsequent fifth to Almaqam there can be forgiven as she was found to be slightly lame behind after.
Progressive 3-time winner in 2025 who looked rusty when third of 8 in handicap at Hamilton (9f, good to firm) 31 days ago. Tongue tie goes on and she should come on for that outing.

Lightly-raced filly who was seen only 3 times last season but was a decent third when fancied for the Ribblesdale at this meeting. Back down to 1m both starts this spring and she left comeback run well behind when landing a listed event at Leopardstown, suited by strong pace. Can do better again.

Hails from a family that has brought plenty of success to connections, including at the highest level, and has looked a bright prospect in winning both his starts to date, latterly 4-runner novice at Haydock (1½m). Step up in trip likely to suit and he's an interesting contender up in grade.

Left debut form well behind and was fairly impressive in 9-runner maiden at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) last month, regardless that he had the perfect trip up the inside and hung across the track when in control. Will go on improving. Bought for £200,000 at the Goffs London Sale on Monday.
Recorded a fifth success of his career in 5-runner handicap at Plumpton (2m, soft) in October. Returns from 8 month-break from a career-high mark but has a good record fresh.

Jack Christopher colt who shaped very well when 2 lengths second of 13 to Celeron in maiden at the Curragh (6f, good) on debut a fortnight ago, the only one of those held up to land any sort of blow. Sure to improve and seemingly yard's first string on jockey bookings.

Territories colt who attracted support and knew job when winning 7-runner maiden at the Curragh (5f, heavy) on debut back in March, just lasting home having gone on entering final 1f. Has since joined powerful connections and is open to improvement.

Progressive filly who completed hat-trick when making all in Sandown listed race last summer. Ended her 3-y-o campaign with an excellent second in Group 1 Sun Chariot at Newmarket and looks set for another good season given how she quickened past Kon Tiki when making a winning return at Goodwood.

Wootton Bassett colt who justified odds-on favouritism in 8-runner maiden at the Curragh (6f, good to firm) last month, leading over 1f out. Sure to progress and demands considerable respect for connections who have won this race 3 times in the past 11 years.
Point winner who took a step forward on his handicap debut when landing 9-runner handicap at Bangor (2½m) 13 months ago. Off since though so has his fitness to prove.
Winner of handicap hurdle at Bangor last autumn. Also placed over fences on next 2 outings (including here) but weakened quickly back from a break at Uttoxeter last month.

C&D winner last summer and proved pretty reliable on all-weather thereafter, scoring at Wolverhampton in October. Poorly drawn when last seen at Lingfield in April but might prove a shade vulnerable here.

Better than ever in 2025, the highlight being a narrow success in 1m Group 3 here in July. Shaped as if still needing the outing when 8¾ lengths fifth of 8 in a listed race at Haydock (10.5f, good to soft) 25 days ago but would need to step up markedly on that to land a handicap of this nature.
Twice a winner on Flat (stays 1½m) in 2024 but below form last year and offered little in a pair of 2m novice hurdles at Hereford and over C&D last month.

Dubawi Legend filly who had shaped quite well on debut and wasn't seen to best effect switched to all-weather/upped in trip when fifth of 6 in novice at Wolverhampton (7f) last month, weakening when badly hampered final 1f. Remains with potential.
A fair Flat winner but a well-held sixth at Haydock (1¼m) 26 days ago. Still needs considering starting out in this sphere though.

Without a win since 2-y-o debut but made the frame 3 times at the highest level last season, including when fourth in Coronation Stakes over C&D at this meeting. All the better for return when good second to Jancis (seen to better effect) in Dahlia at Newmarket. Good chance on form but drawn widest.
Won a 1m Ayr maiden last spring but has barely beaten a rival in 6 handicap outings since. Hard to make a case for unless the market speaks otherwise.
Three-time hurdle winner. Has shown promise when third on 2 of 3 chase outings in recent months and he won't need to pull out much more for a change of headgear (first-time blinkers for cheekpieces).
Churchill filly who made a winning start to her career in 5-runner novice at Kempton (6f) 3 weeks ago, making all to score in cosy fashion. Looks sure to progress and win more races.
Ended his time for Rebecca Menzies with a clear-cut chase debut success at Hexham (2½m, good) 46 days ago. Subsequently sold for £25,000 and joined the best yard in the country.

Progressive in handicaps last season after landing 1¼m Newmarket maiden in May. Not seen to best effect in a slowly-run race behind Radiant Beauty over C&D on her return and she's still the type to do better again, for all low draw isn't ideal.

Lost his way for Eoin Doyle over hurdles in Ireland but resurgent for new yard, winning on return at Thirsk prior to finishing a good second over 2m here in May. Posted another solid effort when third over hurdles at Worcester (2½m, good to soft) latest and he's respected back on the level.

Proving consistent rather than progressive in maidens so far, making the frame for a third time in as many starts when second of 11 at Listowel (6.3f, good) last month. Very tough to see him involved.

Hasn't got his head in front since successful in listed race at Newmarket in November 2023. Not discredited in handicaps both starts this year, 4 lengths sixth of 15 to Classic at Newbury last time, though looks vulnerable in this contest. Cheekpieces back on.

Maiden winner on second start and also landed the Irish Cambridgeshire last summer. Well held on final outing in 2025, but making first run since leaving D. K. Weld he proved better than ever when scoring in impressive style at Naas last month. Interesting contender.

Won 4 of her 5 starts as a 3-y-o, notably the Prix de l'Opera at Longchamp. Missed the following season but was in the process of showing she retains all her ability back from 20 months off at Haydock before her race was ended by putting her foot in a hole. Can make a bold bid if none the worse.

Excellent third to Calandagan and Ombudsman in last year's Champion over C&D and grabbed a Group 1 success of his own in the Tattersalls Gold Cup at the Currragh (10.5f, good) on reappearance. That form looks even better in light of runner-up Bay City Roller's easy Coronation Cup win since.
Distant fifth on Hamilton debut last June but showed a lot more when fourth of 9 at Newcastle 10 months later, despite still looking green. May do better again.

Ended 2025 with a handicap 4-timer over 7f and improved again on return when edged out by Urban Lion in the Lincoln at Doncaster. Ran well when fifth in the Spring Cup at Newbury, before a below-par effort in listed race at Longchamp last month. Needs to get back on the up.

Fairly useful winning hurdler who came good at the third time of asking over fences in 4-runner race at Plumpton (2½m, good to soft) in April. Bit lacklustre when only second of 4 at Newton Abbot (21f, good to soft) since, though.

Took her record to 3 from 4 when scoring at listed level at Chantilly last spring and was a good second to Cheshire Dancer here later in the season. No real impact on her last 4 outings, though, so bit to prove on handicap debut.

Palace Pier colt who was an expensive buy at the breeze-ups and showed plenty to work on despite being a bit uneasy as favourite when second of 6 in novice at Haydock (6f, soft) just under 4 weeks ago, leading briefly last ½f. Sure to have learnt plenty from that and will improve.

Massaat filly who knew her job when third of 6 in maiden at Salisbury (5f, good to soft) on debut last month. Matched that form when fourth of 5 in novice at Bath (5f, good to firm) 8 days later but is out of her depth in this.

Smart mare who has won a Nottingham listed and York Group 2 (for second year in succession) this spring. Good third to Ombudsman last year but surely playing for place money at best again in such a strong renewal.

Several fine efforts in defeat last season and has continued the good work this time around, second under top weight in Newmarket handicap on return and not beaten far (just behind She's Perfect) in listed race at Goodwood. Tough ask here, however, and will need some luck from stall 1.

Modest form when a debut third in Newton Abbot bumper last July. Tongue tied and too free when last in Uttoxeter bumper in October on final run for David Jeffreys. Hooded for hurdling/yard debut here with lots more required.

Stepped forward on her handicap bow when third at Lingfield (1¼m) in December and showed plenty to work on after a 5-month break when fourth of 9 at C&D in May. Poorly placed after reverting to her slow-starting ways back at Lingfield 18 days ago, so others are preferred from 2 lb out of weights.

Successful at Southwell in January but has struggled since. Reverts to turf for the first time this year and, whilst he's yet to win on this surface, he went close over C&D off a similar mark last summer.

Galiway colt who built on his debut promise when staying on well to land a well-run 1½m maiden at Chester last month, well on top finish. Sure to be suited by the still longer trip on that evidence and looks very promising.

Ended 2025 with back-to-back 7f/1m wins Leicester and Newcastle. Took another step forward when a strong-travelling second of 6 at Southwell (1m) on her return in April and ran at least as well with the benefit of a handy position when second to Radiant Beauty at C&D last time. Up another 1 lb here.

Good fifth in an 18-runner Group 3 at Doncaster in September and though she failed to land a blow in listed company on her next 3 starts, she weakened only late after chasing down a pair that got first run at Yarmouth last time. Ran well over C&D in the Sandringham last year and she's shortlisted.

St Mark's Basilica colt who again shaped well when second of 7 in maiden at Leopardstown (7f, good) last month, just unable to hold off a stronger stayer having looked all over a winner turning for home. Remains open to improvement and this return to 6f looks a good move.
Well beaten on all 5 starts.
Promising type. Won 5-runner maiden at Keeneland (5.5f, firm) 54 days ago by 6½ lengths from reopposing Shining Moment. A very interesting contender from the US.

Kodi Bear filly who showed improved form to get off the mark switched to turf in 9-runner maiden at Redcar (6f, good to firm) just over 3 weeks ago. First-time hood goes on and she'll need to improve significantly to have a say.

Hindered by the odd slow start but broke on terms and cashed in on a handy mark with a tongue strap fitted at Wolverhampton 2 weeks ago. Showed a good attitude in the process and retains handicap scope up 4 lb.
Bayside Boy gelding who showed plenty to work on first time up when second of 10 in maiden at Roscommon (7.5f, good) last month. Dropped to a sprint trip immediately and he's open to improvement.
Fair form. Won 6f maiden at Wolverhampton in May but her subsequent fifth of 9 in 5f Chantilly listed event suggests she's unlikely to be up to the required standard here.

Dubawi colt out of a 4-time Group 1 winner. Knew more than on debut and clearly benefited from the longer trip when winning 10-runner novice at Thirsk (7f, good) last month. Has a way to go to live up to his pedigree but looks sure to go on improving.

Night of Thunder filly who ran a remarkable race pitched straight into pattern company when neck second of 6 to Victorious in Group 3 at Naas (6f, good to soft) on debut last month, though chance she might have been a bit flattered having challenged closest to stand rail. Clear pick on form.
9/1, sixth of 9 in maiden at Haydock (6f, good to soft) on debut 26 days ago. Needs to leave that well behind.
240,000 gns breezer who justified market support with ease on her 5f Lingfield debut (good to firm) 18 days ago. Looks sure to progress but James Doyle sides with Wild Blossom.

Held form well last season, good second in the Kensington Palace (straight track) at this meeting before a narrow winner of 4-runner Group 3 at Leopardstown. Typically gave her running on comeback run but likely to find a few too strong here.

Bumper winner in Ireland and 2-3 over hurdles in Britain after maiden/novice wins in recent months, looking well suited by a step up to 2¾m at Stratford (good to soft) last time. Slightly shorter trip now but his opening mark looks lenient.
Acted as a pacemaker in last month's Lockinge and he's presumably here to fulfil the same role for Minnie Hauk.

Useful at his best on Flat. Much improved from hurdling debut when second in 2m conditions event at Ascot in January. Not in same form in Naas juvenile after for Denis Hogan but fit from the Flat and sets a very high standard starting out for new yard here.
Made it 2-2 when an impressive winner of a listed race at Newmarket last spring. However, disappointed in 3 starts since, looking a difficult ride (pulls hard).

Generally progressive in 2025 and took another step forward when digging deep for success in the Lincoln at Doncaster on return. However, shaped as if amiss when well held in Spring Cup at Newbury last time, reported to have lost a shoe.

Out of a Group 3 winner in France and won by a street on his introduction in a Newcastle novice (1m) in March. Found the Feilden Stakes coming too soon in his development next time and made short work of the drop back in grade at Salisbury (1¼m). Likely to stay 1¾m and remains open to improvement.

Without a win since debut but produced best effort when runner-up in listed race at Naas last spring. However, well held both subsequent outings, in the Jersey at this meeting on first occasion. Off 9 months ahead of first run since leaving G. M. Lyons. Hood applied.

Won at Downpatrick last season but largely out of sorts after. Hinted at a revival in 3m handicap hurdle there last month though (in touch when brought down 2 out) on final run for John Joseph Hanlon. Not without interest for new yard, especially if the market vibes are positive.
Both starts at Gulfstream, finishing second on dirt before going one better on fast turf 23 days later. Wears blinkers. Likely capable of better with Christophe Soumillon doing the steering.
Remains winless but she comes here on the back of a respectable fourth of 6 in handicap hurdle over C&D 26 days ago.
Fairly useful on the Flat (scored at Yarmouth in April) and made an encouraging start in this sphere with second of 6 in novice at Huntingdon (2m) 23 days ago. Open to progress.
Smart performer but surely in here as a pacemaker for Ombudsman.

Placed in maiden hurdles in 2024 and runner-up in a 2m handicap chase at Ayr in January on his final start for Stuart Crawford. Remote fourth back hurdling at Hereford for new yard 6 weeks ago and has since undergone a breathing operation.
Has shown some promise all 3 starts since switched to hurdles, fifth of 12 in 2m Taunton novice in March. Likely seen in a better light now going into handicaps after a break.

3-time winner in France for M. Delzangles in 2025 and ended the year with placed efforts at listed/Group 3 level. Making second start for present stable, wasn't ideally placed in a Meydan handicap (9.5f) when last seen in February, though faces a difficult task here.
Overcame inexperience to win 6-runner novice at Thirsk (5f) on her debut but disappointed behind a few of these in the Marygate at York since.

In top form at Worcester last summer, winning twice and runner-up 3 times. Stepped up on recent run when fourth of 7 at Warwick but ran badly back over C&D last month and has since undergone a breathing operation.

300,000 gns breeze-up purchase who looked something out of the ordinary when bolting up by 10 lengths from Crownbreaker on her 5f Carlisle debut (soft) last month, the same race the stable won with Venetian Sun before she took last year's Albany. A bold show looks assured.

Foaled April 30. Belardo filly. Sister to winner up to 1m Prairie Falcon and half-sister to 3 winners, including 1m winner Falcon's Vision and 2-y-o 1m winner Perregrin. Most newcomers from the yard are better for a run.

Proved disappointing over fences given he looked the type to take well to that discipline but returned to form when capitalising on a falling mark on second start back in this sphere at Bangor (17f) last month, seeming suited by a return to patient tactics. A 7 lb higher mark is manageable.

Won 3 times at up to 6f in 2025 (twice over C&D). Hasn't hit the same heights this year and little encouragement to be gleaned from effort at this course last month, but has been given a chance by the handicapper and any market support should be taken seriously.
Tremendous record at Ripon and arrives on the back of a good second of 6 at Catterick 18 days ago. Still 4 lb above last winning mark but demands a second look whenever he runs at this track.

Continued to improve last season, winning at Haydock before a fine effort upped to this trip in the Sandringham over C&D, not so well placed as a couple who beat her. Not given a hard time when fifth at Thirsk (1m) on return fitted with tongue tie, though low draw here has to temper enthusiasm.

Promising third on Newmarket debut but slammed by Wild Blossom at Carlisle since. Perhaps the soft ground was against her in Cumbria but hard to fancy after that even though David Egan seemingly prefers her to Lover Girl.

Improved when coming from rear to land a York handicap (9f) in September and matched that form when a close third in a listed race at Milan the following month, but this looks a very stiff task on return from 8 months off.

4-time winner in France and made the frame in a Group 3 in Milan in October. However, he failed to come on for seasonal/stable debut when 6¼ lengths tenth of 18 to Mister Winston in handicap at Epsom 12 days ago, albeit racing closer to pace than ideal.
Made all on Goodwood debut and useful effort when caught only in the dying strides by Love A Giggle in 5f York listed event a fortnight later. Should be more to come.

Sioux Nation filly who looked good when making it 2-2 in a 5f Curragh listed race (good) last month but beaten 6½ lengths into fourth by Victorious in 6f Naas Group 3 a fortnight later. Quickly reverts to 5f.

Ended 2025 on the up, landing back-to-back Goodwood handicaps in the autumn and third in listed race at Nottingham on final outing. Has picked up where he left off in 2 starts this spring, beaten only a neck in 18-runner contest at York last month, though has career-high mark to overcome.

Bagged a C&D handicap for second successive season in May and stepped up again when just unable to repel his odds-on stablemate (who won a competitive York handicap on Friday) at Pontefract (1½m) 9 days ago. Front-running style well suited to this venue and he should take some catching again.

Winner on the Flat/over hurdles for Joseph O'Brien, though has shaped like one with problems over hurdles since joining present yard and did nothing to dispel that notion back on the Flat at Salisbury last month.

Kodi Bear colt who knew what was required when providing his trainer with a third Brocklesby in 5 years in March. That form hasn't really worked out, and he failed to meet expectations when down the field in a listed race at Sandown (5f, good) just under 3 weeks ago. Now upped in trip.

Won the 2024 Summer Plate at Market Rasen and took advantage of a reduced mark at the same venue last autumn. Off since and got to be a chance he's using this return to hurdles as a prep for this year's Summer Plate.

Ended a losing run from a 6 lb higher mark at Chester (12.3f) 13 months ago and in better heart than form figures suggest towards the back end of last year on all-weather. Reappears for new yard back at a more suitable trip and interesting if supported in the betting down in class.

No match for the reopposing More Champagne on debut but showed the benefit of that experience with a 3-length win at Churchill Downs (5f, firm) 4 weeks later. Wears blinkers. One of 2 for Wesley Ward.
Former Paul Nicholls inmate who hasn't shown much for some time, including both runs for his new yard at Chepstow and Cartmel this spring. First-time hood now tried.
Placed in Grade 1 company as a novice. Started last season with a win and second in 23f Uttoxeter handicaps but has largely struggled since, including well held back at Uttoxeter last month.
Made a winning start to her career in 8-runner maiden at Chantilly (5f, soft) 36 days ago. Likely to progress for her top French yard

Took his form up a notch in handicaps last year, easily making all at Newmarket in November to end the campaign. Repeated the feat in 24-runner Spring Cup at Newbury on return, scoring by ¾ length from Classic, though tougher ask to pull off the same tactics here.

3-time winner last year and added to his tally at Southwell in January. Confirmed himself a smart performer with runner-up efforts at Newcastle on Good Friday and in the Thirsk Hunt Cup, though needs to bounce back from a lesser effort in race won by Classic at Newbury last time.

Better known for all-weather exploits (already won 4 times this year) but brought along steadily in this sphere and appeals as a likely improver now handicapping on the back of fourth placings in 2m novices at Hereford and Ludlow. Likely player.
Long-standing maiden who can only be watched returning after 16 months off.

Bayside Boy colt who was favoured by the betting over those with experience and showed why when winning 6-runner maiden at Hamilton (5f, firm) 3 weeks ago, quickening to lead entering final 1f. Open to a fair amount of improvement with Murphy booked to ride.

Foaled January 30. Sands of Mali filly. Dam, 6f winner, closely related to useful 2-y-o 8.3f winner Wise Prince. Newcomer from a respected yard. Would enter calculations if the betting vibes are strong.
Really smart miler (including fourth in last month's Lockinge) but he'll need to advance his form significantly for a step up in trip if he's to play a leading role here.
Hit the frame on 3 occasions earlier in her career but is of little account these days.

Low-mileage filly who was successful on second of 3 starts in novice company and best effort yet when second on handicap debut at Newcastle (12.5f) in November. Possibly unsuited by fast ground on reappearance at Haydock (10.5f) in April and better anticipated now back up in trip.

French challenger who picked up a Group 2 at Chantilly last summer and was also a good 2¼ lengths fourth of 13 to Fallen Angel in Prix Rothschild at Deauville. Unlucky not to make a winning return in listed event at Longchamp and she's not to be underestimated.
Fair form on both starts, stepping up on 5f Newmarket debut when second of 6 in novice at Windsor (6f, good) 6 weeks ago. Sets a decent standard and has the rail draw.
Capitalised on a reduced mark to bag 6-runner handicap hurdle over C&D 20 days ago. Back up 4 lb but he's expected to be bang there.

A fair 1m2f Flat winner who opened his account in this sphere at Stratford last June and backed it up with two solid efforts there and at Uttoxeter last July. Should strip sharper for a recent Flat run at Chester so enters calculations.
9/2, hinted at promise with fifth of 7 in bumper at Plumpton (2¼m, soft) on debut 100 days ago. In top hands so this son of Jack Hobbs can do better now going over hurdles.

Excellent second in listed event at Chantilly last July on her final outing for Paul Attwater. Returned from 9 months off with a good third in Kempton listed contest (1¼m) in April and was out of her depth in the Gordon Richards Stakes last time but others make more appeal back in a handicap.
Modest maiden under both codes. Hood refitted and back on track with fourth of 8 in handicap hurdle at Huntingdon (2m) 29 days ago. Needs to back it up with headgear retained.

Top-class performer who burst onto the Group 1 scene when showing a potent turn of foot to land this last year. Added the International at York in August and has returned to win the Dubai Turf and Brigadier Gerard this spring. A bold bid looks assured.
In frame 4 of last 5 starts, ½-length third of 9 to Ganthorpe in 6f handicap at Carlisle on latest. Tackles 5f for the first time now and should find a race.

Improved form when making all in listed race at York (1¼m, good) last summer and good second in Group 3 at the Curragh next time. Below par at Group 2/listed level both starts so far this season, but mark looks workable if first-time blinkers spark a revival on this belated handicap debut.

Unlucky second in Britannia at this meeting last year. Eye-catching return when fourth in Lincoln Trial at Wolverhampton but hasn't confirmed that promise since, though was switched to making the running in listed race at Goodwood (1¼m) last time. No surprise to see a bold show back over 1m here.

Has yet to offer much over hurdles, capitulating tamely again in this headgear combination last time. The fact he was runner-up on sole outing in Irish points provides some hope now chasing but it's still hard to be confident.

Capitalised on easing mark at Wetherby in April and, having met trouble in running next time, she's confirmed she's in top form with further wins at Redcar and this C&D 2 weeks ago. Up 7 lb for that decisive success but clearly deserves utmost respect in current mood.

Lope de Vega colt who improved with each run as at 2 yrs. Cheekpieces fitted when a good third of 8 on his handicap debut/reappearance at Newmarket (1¼m) prior to opening his account in 1½m maiden at Salisbury. Likely to stay this still longer trip but has plenty on at the weights.
Progressing with experience in this sphere and posted a good second of 10 in Sedgefield maiden in February. Scored on the Flat at Doncaster 12 days ago so looks the one to beat.

New Bay colt who continues to rise through the ranks, taking the step up in class and distance in his stride as he completed the hat-trick in 5-runner listed race at Navan (13f, good to soft) last month, albeit aided by a well-judged ride. Has a likeable attitude and one to keep on right side of.
Dual hurdles winner in spring 2024 for Paddy Butler. In good nick over hurdles since joining David Brace, fourth of 7 in handicap at Stratford (2m) 31 days ago. Considered.

Took a step back in right direction despite being slowly away when 5½ lengths fourth of 10 to Lillie Margot in handicap at Nottingham last time. Steps up in trip with first-time blinkers replacing visor worn then.
A fair 2m hurdles winner for James Owen last June but yet to fire for new stable and retried in a visor when pulled up in handicap hurdle at Hereford (2½m) 62 days ago.

Useful handicapper who returned with a good fourth in Spring Mile at Doncaster and against several unexposed rivals, proved at least as good as ever when second of 11 at Thirsk (1m, good, 15/2) 17 days ago. Not ruled out.

Highly tried after winning Southwell handicap over 1½m on last year's return. Tailed off in listed race at Goodwood (1½m, good) on yard debut/reappearance and was ridden too aggressively at Hamilton last time, but all of her best form comes over much longer trips. New headgear.
Creditable efforts when third twice in April and had excuses when only sixth at Redcar on penultimate outing. Disappointing last time but place claims if able to shrug that effort off.

Fair winner on Flat (up to 2m) in 2025 for George Boughey. Progressing with experience in this sphere and posted a very good third of 14 in novice hurdle at Chepstow (2m) 54 days ago. Since had a breathing operation and not out of things on his handicap debut.

Zarak gelding from the family of top-class winner up to 1½m Azamour who has improved with each run to date, opening account in 1¼m Leopardstown maiden in April before finishing second of 5 to Limestone in 13f listed race at Navan. Step up to 1¾m may unlock more with first-time cheekpieces applied.

Won first 3 starts, completing hat-trick in York listed race last spring. Underwhelming seventh in Coronation Stakes at this meeting final 3-y-o start but made an encouraging comeback after 11 months off when ¾-length second to Blue Bolt in listed race at Goodwood. Can build on that.

Wootton Bassett filly who is 2-2 over 6f at Naas, latterly a Group 3 by a neck from highly promising newcomer Controlla, with the pair 6 lengths clear of the third. The drop to 5f poses a different question but she's a very exciting prospect.

All 4 career victories at Dundalk but posted a career best when runner-up in Group 2 at the Curragh last month. However, she was seen to good effect from the front that day and will find this much harder.

Lucky Vega filly who was 1¼ lengths second of 8 to Pershaada in novice at Goodwood (5f, good) on debut 26 days ago, finishing with running left. Open to progress. Bought for £380,000 at the Goffs London Sale on Monday.
Signs of ability in 3 all-weather outings over 6f in April, catching the eye of the stewards after finishing with running left on the third occasion. Capable of better at some point.
Harry Angel gelding who finished a close second over 7f at Newcastle (novice on all-weather) and Catterick (maiden on good to firm) last month. Should have the speed for 6f. Leading claims.

Progressive filly, completing a hat-trick on her handicap debut at Kempton in February. Likely better still to come, though this is her first start on turf and it's a competitive environment to be pitched into after 126 days off.

Progressive at 2 yrs without winning and has continued on an upward trajectory this season, comfortably landing the odds in a 1¼m novice at Yarmouth on his return and just touch off in a small-field listed event at Goodwood (11f) on most recent outing. Step up to 1¾m not certain to suit, though.

Had Bint Archange and Havana Lightning behind her when making a winning debut in 8-runner maiden at Newmarket (5f, good) in April but she went backwards from that when 4¾ lengths fourth of 8 to Pershaada at Goodwood (5f, good) since.

Cracksman colt who left debut form well behind to open his account in 12-runner maiden at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month, responding well to assert final 100 yds. Likely to progress further but he'll need another significant step forward to get involved.

Back-to-back novice winner last year and made a successful handicap debut at Haydock in August. Runner-up at Group 3/listed level on final 2 outings but hasn't matched that form so far this season, failing to come on for reappearance when third in listed race at Leopardstown in May.

Bagged a pair of 6f novice events at Ayr and Redcar last summer. Has failed to kick on since but easily best effort in handicaps when third of 13 at Thirsk over 6f 12 days ago. Has now found his level.
